panel.summary: Empty-data guard is key-count based, so a data object whose only keys are undefined still bumps `updatedAt`
panel.evidence: `Object.keys(data).length > 0 ? { ...data, updatedAt: new Date() } : data` counts keys, not defined values. `ApiV1DocumentsController.update` (api/v1/documents.controller.ts:79) passes the request body straight through as `data`, so a body such as `{"title":null}` or any unrecognized key yields length>0 and re-sorts the document to the top of the list (and, for an unknown key, Prisma throws afterwards). The new spec only covers `{}` and `{title:'New'}`, so this branch is untested.

coderabbit.summary: Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.detail: **Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.** When `data` is empty, the current code calls `prisma.document.update({ data: {}, where })`. Prisma 6.6.0 may reject an empty `data` object at the client-validation level or generate invalid SQL (an `UPDATE` with no `SET` columns). The test mocks `prisma.document.update` so it wouldn't catch a real runtime failure. Returning the existing row via `findUniqueOrThrow` avoids the risk entirely and skips a needless write.
